title: Release wrapper for clean computations
statement: Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine, let $entry,exit$ be states of $C$, and let $result$ and $emit$ map binary words to binary words. Let $B:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and suppose $C$ has a positive number of work tapes. Assume that for every binary input $x$ and argument word $arg$, there is a time $t\le B(|arg|)$ with $t>0$ such that at every time $v$ with $0<v<t$ the machine has not reached $exit$, and at time $t$ its configuration is the seam configuration with state $exit$, tape words encoding $result(arg)$, and output $emit(arg)$. Then the release wrapper of $C$ satisfies the clean contract for $result$ and $emit$ with budget $n\mapsto B(n)+1$.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a finite binary Turing machine
$result,emit$ map binary words to binary words
$B$ maps natural numbers to natural numbers
$C$ has a positive number of work tapes
For every binary input and argument, a time $t\le B(|arg|)$ exists with $t>0$
At each $v$ with $0<v<t$, the run has not reached $exit$
At time $t$, the configuration has state $exit$, tape words encoding $result(arg)$, and output $emit(arg)$
replaced: If a machine has, for every input and argument, a positive first exit within a budget $B$ at the canonical seam with a result word and emitted chunk, then its release wrapper satisfies the uniform clean contract with budget $B + 1$; the minimal-halt cut retains the entire clean configuration.
